baer-heitev.1#א: To rinse. Shach wrote it is plain that one also needs wiping, but the Rav abbreviated in language; and Ran wrote one need not wait six hours from the time they remove it but from eating; and it is written in Tur Chaadash general rule 76 law 1 that the same applies regarding the custom of waiting one hour.
baer-heitev.1#ב: And recited Birkat HaMazon. Maharshal wrote that according to all, if one did not clear the table and recite Birkat HaMazon, even the entire day is forbidden, for this requires another meal; and many people are lenient in this and it is an error in their hands, end of his words. And it appears that if one ate meat without a meal he must recite the final blessing first, and otherwise it is not clearing — Shach. (And the same applies also to one who practices even regarding meat after cheese in Birkat HaMazon and in clearing: if he ate cheese without a meal he must recite the final blessing first — such is the case.)
baer-heitev.1#ג: One hour. Taz wrote in name of Maharai that the scrupulous withdraw their hands from the morning meal until the evening meal; and ShaDa wrote [Maharshal] that in any case among Torah scholars it is fit to protest and rebuke them that they should not be lenient less than six hours; and in any case even one who practices leniency to wait only one hour also needs wiping and rinsing. And those who recite Birkat HaMazon in order to eat cheese afterward act against the Gemara, for they permitted Birkat HaMazon only when one clears himself from that meal; but these prepare themselves for another eating — if so Birkat HaMazon does not help at all; and one who fears the word of God should refrain from sitting with them in one gathering.
baer-heitev.1#ד: His teeth. Shach wrote that one also needs wiping and rinsing; but certainly if he did not find meat between his teeth, the custom of waiting one hour suffices even without wiping and rinsing — and so they practice, end of his words.
baer-heitev.2#א: That he examine. Shach wrote that the same applies at night if he has a good lamp like a torch — he need not rinsing; however Rif wrote [R' Peretz] that one should wash them even by day, because sometimes the cheese is fatty and sticks to the moisture of the hands without his knowledge; and Atzei Etz Chaim wrote that so they practice. (And Peri Chadash wrote that one who eats with a fork, whether by day or night, need not rinsing.)
baer-heitev.2#ב: To wash them. Specifically in water rinsing helps, but not in other liquids — Shach.
baer-heitev.2#ג: And to rinse it. One need not be precise whether mouth-wiping or rinsing comes first — whichever he wishes he may do first.
baer-heitev.2#ד: Fowl. Shach wrote that even though meat of wild animal too is only d'rabbanan, nevertheless since its meat resembles that of domestic animal they were stringent with it.
baer-heitev.2#ה: To be stringent. Shach wrote that Maharshal picked a quarrel with those who are stringent that it is like heresy, and his words are not compelling. And Taz wrote in name of Orach Chaim that the measure of hard cheese that Rama mentioned means that six months passed on it or that it is wormy; and specifically with wormy cheese one should be stringent; but if it is not wormy and was not made from milk that was set in the stomach but from mere milk and dried out, or one eats butter — one should not be stringent in this more than wiping, cleaning teeth, rinsing, and rinsing hands, except for one who practices abstinence and scrupulousness, end of his words. And Shach wrote in name of Mitzaref LeChochmah that according to what they practice to wait one hour, it is possible the Zohar too agrees that it is forbidden only in one meal [and in one time], and the language of the Zohar in parashat Mishpatim so appears.
baer-heitev.3#א: And fat. Taz wrote in name of a sage that even with goose fat one should be stringent so; and Beit Yosef in Orach Chaim siman 173 wrote that meat broth has the law of a meat dish since it is clear, but if it is thick like vegetables it has the law of meat, end of his words.
baer-heitev.3#ב: In a pot. Shach wrote below siman 95 it will be explained that even to eat it with cheese is permitted, for it is noten taam bar noten taam; and it appears that what it teaches us here that it is permitted to eat cheese afterward is even if it was cooked in a pot that was not rinsed well, for there is a bit of substance of prohibition — in such a case it is forbidden to eat it with cheese as explained there — and here it is permitted, end of his words. (And I do not understand what he wrote that even to eat it with cheese is permitted as noten taam bar noten taam — for Rama there forbids, see there.)
baer-heitev.3#ג: Between them. Shach wrote that even by day, according to all, cheese sticks more to the hands than cheese itself.
baer-heitev.3#ד: Waiter. Shach disagrees on this, for Rashi in chapter Kol HaBasar does not appear so, but only regarding netilat yadayim at the meal for eating, as written in Orach Chaim siman 163; but intermediate waters between a dish and cheese or the reverse — the reason is that it sticks to the hands — it is plain there is no difference between eater and one who touches. (And Peri Chadash wrote it is reasonable that if one carries and brings the food placed in the bowl, he need not rinsing, see there.)
baer-heitev.4#א: Sticking. Taz wrote that this refers to what was written that one wants to cut cheese with a meat knife; but what was written that it is forbidden to cut bread, etc. — one need only wipe the knife, as Beit Yosef wrote, for it is noten taam bar noten taam; and for us one need not this, for it is explained in siman 96 that specifically with a sharp thing they say it absorbs because of pressure of the knife, end of his words. And Shach wrote that Maharshal forbids cutting bread with it to eat with cheese even if they stuck it in the ground; and he challenged him, for the halachah is that if one cut bread with a meat knife its taste was nullified in the bread and it is permitted to cut with it even a radish to eat it in kutach as below end of seif 96. (And I say one may resolve that one who investigates Maharshal's words appears that certainly it is permitted to cut bread with a meat knife through sticking to eat with cheese; but Maharshal deals with a meat knife that is forbidden l'chatchila to stick in the ground to eat cheese itself with it — investigate.)
baer-heitev.4#ב: Knives. Shach wrote at a time of pressure when he has no other knife we establish the law for it; and Taz wrote that according to the custom it is forbidden to cut cheese with a meat knife even through sticking in the ground; but nevertheless to cut bread with it to eat cheese — in this we may well rely on wiping it first, end of his words. (And Bach wrote specifically at a time of pressure, such as when he is on the road and has no other knife — then it is permitted to cut bread with a meat knife and eat with cheese — and so Shach.)

beer-hagolah.1#א: Statement of Rav Chisda — Chullin daf 105.
beer-hagolah.1#ב: Rambam chapter 9 of Forbidden Foods and Rashba in Torat HaBayit and in name of great authors, end of section.
beer-hagolah.1#ג: There in the Gemara like Mar Ukva and as Rosh and Rambam explain there.
beer-hagolah.2#א: Like the plain meaning of R' Yochanan to R' Asi there.
beer-hagolah.2#ב: Like Rav Yitzchak son of Rav Mesharshia there daf 104.
beer-hagolah.2#ג: There in the Gemara from the precision of the tanna of Agra, etc.
beer-hagolah.2#ד: Baraita of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel there.
beer-hagolah.2#ח: There in name of Rambam from what the tanna of Agra taught there, and per his explanation meaning specifically cheese and afterward fowl.
beer-hagolah.3#_: Statement of Rav Nachman Chullin daf 105. And per Tosafot in name of Rabbenu Tam: since meat and cheese are not in substance and there is only taste, they were not stringent that it be obligatory to wash hands.
beer-hagolah.4#א: Tur in siman 91 from Yerushalmi and Hagahot Ashiri in name of Or Zarua.
beer-hagolah.4#ב: Responsum of Ramban siman 172 (and Rashba siman 77).

siftei-kohen.1#א: ["Even meat of wild animal and fowl. Meaning that they are d'rabbanan, as written in siman 87:"]
siftei-kohen.1#ב: ["Until he waits, etc. — so wrote Tur: and within the six hours, even if there is no meat between the teeth it is forbidden, because meat expels fat and draws taste for a long time; and therefore the reason if they did not eat but only chewed for a child, need not wait, since they did not eat it does not impart taste; and Rambam gave a reason for waiting because of meat between the teeth, and one who chews for a child must wait; and it is good to follow the stringencies of both reasons, end of his words. And Mechaber's words were explained, and the elder Taz wrote: within the time, even if there is no meat between the teeth it is forbidden because meat expels fat and expels taste for a long time; and therefore if they did not eat but only chewed for a child must wait — even though they did not eat, nevertheless taste of the meat remained in his mouth and drew for him taste of fat as if he ate, end of his words — and his words are astonishing:"]
siftei-kohen.1#ג: ["And removes it. Ran wrote need not wait six hours from the time of removal but from eating; and it is written in Tur Chaadash general rule 76 law 1 that the same applies regarding the custom of waiting one hour:"]
siftei-kohen.1#ד: ["Must rinse his mouth. And Ran wrote that mouth-wiping is required and he did not mention rinsing the mouth; and so Beit Yosef copied in Orach Chaim there and in Tur Chaadash — meaning he follows his reasoning that generally we do not require rinsing the mouth; but for us who require rinsing the mouth, as Taz wrote in seif 2, the same applies here; and therefore the Rav wrote must rinse his mouth, and it is plain that wiping is also required — only he abbreviated in language. It appears to me:"]
siftei-kohen.1#ה: ["And some say, etc. — reason for their dispute: it is found in the Gemara chapter 25 that after meat it is forbidden to eat cheese until another meal; and the view of the first reasoned opinion is from the measure of time from the morning meal until the evening meal, which is six hours; and the view of the second opinion is immediately when one cleared and recited Birkat HaMazon it is called another meal; and Maharshal wrote there that according to all, if one did not clear and recite Birkat HaMazon, even the entire day is forbidden, for we require another meal; and many people are lenient in this and it is an error in their hands, end of his words. And what the Rav wrote in the gloss: but without Birkat HaMazon the waiting of one hour is not precise — if so the entire day is forbidden until one cleared and recited:"]
siftei-kohen.1#ו: ["And recited Birkat HaMazon. It appears that if one ate meat without a meal he must recite the final blessing first, and otherwise it is not clearing:"]
siftei-kohen.1#ז: ["Must pick and remove it. And it was already explained in s.k. 4 that rinsing and mouth-wiping are required; but certainly if he did not find meat between his teeth, the custom of waiting one hour suffices even without wiping and rinsing — and so in Orach Chaim there law 4, and they bring it in Tur Chaadash for halachic ruling, and so it is. And what the Rav wrote: some say immediately if one cleared and recited Birkat HaMazon it is permitted through wiping and rinsing — it appears wiping and rinsing are in any case required, meaning if he comes to eat immediately after he cleared and recited; and the words of Lechem Chamudot (daf 218a) are not understood to me in this:"]
siftei-kohen.1#ח: ["And so it is fit to do. And so Maharshal — that it is fit to do for anyone who has fragrance of Torah, see there:"]
siftei-kohen.2#א: ["Provided he examines his hands. And Rivash wrote the same applies at night if he has a good lamp — need not netilat yadayim; and he brings it Beit Yosef in Orach Chaim there; and it appears he specified a good lamp, but with an ordinary lamp netilat yadayim is required as it appears in the Gemara and poskim; and Maharshal there siman 10 explained more: a good lamp like a torch; however Tur wrote in name of Rif that one should wash them even by day, because sometimes cheese is fatty and sticks to the moisture of the hands without his knowledge — and so is the view of the Acharonim, and so Atzei Etz Chaim — that so they practice:"]
siftei-kohen.2#ב: ["Must wash them. And Beit Yosef wrote in Orach Chaim siman 173, and so: it is written in Orach Chaim in name of Raavad that all matters practiced for mayim acharonim are practiced for intermediate waters between cheese and a dish, whether to be lenient or stringent — except rubbing on the body or wall or distraction, which disqualify intermediate waters but not mayim acharonim, because he still wishes to eat and his hands need guarding; and except drying the hands, for intermediate waters also require drying like the first waters; and except other liquids that are not valid for intermediate waters because they are oily and clear and do not clean the fat and food, end of his words — and so Tur Chaadash there; but Maharshal there disagreed and wrote: since all liquids are valid for mayim acharonim to clean filth, all the more they clean and remove moisture of food, end of his words. And it is not worthwhile in this reasoning to reject Raavad's words and those who follow him, especially to be lenient in a matter without any effort. And the law of mayim acharonim see Orach Chaim siman 181:"]
siftei-kohen.2#ג: ["And must wipe his mouth and rinse it. And Hagahot Maimoniyot wrote in name of Maharam that one need not be precise about mouth-wiping and rinsing — whichever he wishes he may do first, end of his words — and Beit Yosef brings it there:"]
siftei-kohen.2#ד: ["Except groats. So too Tur, and it appears that for all groats it is not wiping; and so appears in Hagahot Ashiri and all poskim. And one may wonder at what Tur Chaadash wrote: except groats of barley — and further in the Gemara chapter 25 (daf 105a) it explicitly appears that for all groats it is forbidden, see there — and it is plain that there is a printing error in Tur there and in Levush there did not notice this and wrote like Tur's language there:"]
siftei-kohen.2#ה: ["And afterward he rinses his mouth. Not precise that the same applies if he precedes rinsing — as written in s.k. 11 — and so Beit Yosef himself in Orach Chaim there on Tur's language which is like Mechaber's language:"]
siftei-kohen.2#ו: ["In meat of domestic animal and wild animal. And even though wild animal is only d'rabbanan, since its meat resembles that of domestic animal they were stringent with it:"]
siftei-kohen.2#ז: ["That whenever the cheese is hard. And from the presumption, if it is aged six months it is considered hard — and so is stated in Tur Chaadash there law 12:"]
siftei-kohen.2#ח: ["Do not eat, etc. And it is written in Mitzaref LeChochmah daf 27a: per what was explained in seif 8 that after eating meat they practice waiting one hour — if so it is possible the Zohar too agrees it is forbidden only in one meal and one time — investigate, end of his words; and the language of the Zohar in parashat Mishpatim so appears, see there:"]
siftei-kohen.2#ט: ["However it is good to be stringent. And Maharshal there picked a quarrel with those who are stringent that it is like heresy; and he said specifically Maharam who had a stumbling block once was stringent, but one who did not have a mishap cannot be stringent, see there — his words are not compelled; and on the contrary in Maharam's words there it appears the opposite, see there — investigate:"]
siftei-kohen.3#א: ["And fat of meat, etc. And even fat of fowl has the law of actual fat — so too Tur Chaadash there law 4 in name of Mordechai and Hagahot ShaDa, and so in Tur Chaadash's simanim there:"]
siftei-kohen.3#ב: ["However if there is no meat, etc. — permitted. Below beginning of siman 95 it will be explained that even to eat it with cheese is permitted as noten taam bar noten taam; and it appears what it teaches us here that it is permitted to eat cheese afterward is even if it was cooked in a pot that was not rinsed well, for there is a bit of substance of prohibition — in such a case it is forbidden to eat it with cheese as explained there — and here it is permitted:"]
siftei-kohen.3#ג: ["However one should wash his hands between them. Even by day, according to all, cheese sticks more to the hands than cheese itself — so agreed the poskim as written in Tur Chaadash there law 3:"]
siftei-kohen.3#ד: ["Waiter who serves, etc. So too Beit Yosef in name of Rashi chapter 25 (daf 107b); and in truth they did not analyze at all, for Rashi does not deal there except regarding netilat yadayim of first waters for eating — and it is plain in the Gemara there and agreed by all poskim as explained in Orach Chaim siman 163 that the feeder need not netilat yadayim even though he touches; but intermediate waters between a dish and cheese or the reverse — the reason is that it sticks to the hands — it is plain there is no difference between eater and one who touches, and no poskim should be omitted to divide in this:"]
siftei-kohen.4#_: However through sticking in hard ground it is permitted. It appears that if they stuck it in hard ground it is permitted l'chatchila to cut bread with it to eat with cheese — and so appears from Orach Chaim and Kol Bo there, and so Tur Chaadash there law 7 explicitly; and Maharshal chapter 25 siman 8 forbids cutting bread with it to eat with cheese even if they stuck it — for they permitted sticking only if it happened by chance that they cut with a meat knife or the reverse that sticking is needed to remove the prohibition — not in such a case, end of his words. And it is difficult, for the halachah is that if one cut bread with a meat knife its taste was nullified in the bread and it is permitted to cut with it even a radish to eat in kutach as below end of seif 96 — and as Maharshal himself wrote there siman 61 — and all the more other things that are not sharp; and it is certain that sticking is better than cutting bread. And it is astonishing, for in the Gemara end of Avodah Zarah and in all poskim it is explicit that even with a gentile's knife it is permitted to eat a radish l'chatchila through sticking — and below siman 121 it is explained that even to cut a sharp thing suffices with this. However one may say in this: since the knife is of a gentile which is already forbidden, therefore sticking is considered to remove it from prohibition — and all this by law; but already all Israel practice to have two knives, as the Rav wrote in the gloss; and at a time of pressure when he has no other knife we establish the law for it — and see what Bach wrote on this; and for now as written.

turei-zahav.1#א: Until he waits six hours. There are two reasons here: first, that meat expels fat and draws taste for a long time — and therefore one who only chews for a child need not wait; second is Rambam's reason because of meat between the teeth, which is called meat until six hours and afterward is like digested — and therefore the chewer is liable to wait; only there is a leniency in meat between the teeth after six hours; and the halachah is to be stringent like both reasons.
turei-zahav.1#ב: After eating meat one hour. So wrote Maharai: many make a compromise of their own to wait one hour after the meat meal when they cleared and recited Birkat HaMazon and eat cheese — even though we find no hint for this measure, nevertheless who will protest them since Tosafot and Ra'avyah permit (Explanation: this is the view of the second opinion that need not wait six hours that Rama brought below); but the scrupulous withdraw from the morning meal to the evening meal; also people practice no difference between fowl and domestic animal; and Maharshal chapter 25 siman 9 wondered why they were lenient against Rif and Rambam who required at least six hours; and ShaDa wrote they practice like Rambam and not like Tosafot who permit; nevertheless clearing and Birkat HaMazon are required, for otherwise even if he waited all day it is forbidden; and he wrote further: if impossible to protest people who are not Torah scholars, but among Torah scholars it is fit to protest and rebuke them not to be lenient less than six hours, end of his words — and he expanded; and in Levush: this waiting one hour that Rama mentioned is from Semag and it is a printing error — no poskim wrote so, only Maharai and Orach Chaim wrote the world practices so but not that the law is so; and it is plain that one who practices this leniency to wait one hour also needs wiping and rinsing as mentioned in the words of the second opinion of Rama from which this leniency spread.
turei-zahav.1#ג: But they are not scrupulous in this. I do not know what they rely on, for the essence of the leniency is that they hold like the second opinion Rama mentioned, which is Tosafot and Ra'avyah's view as Maharai wrote above — and there in Tosafot's explanation in this language: even immediately if one cleared and recited Birkat HaMazon it is fine, end of his words — it appears Birkat HaMazon helps only when he already cleared himself from the meat meal; but here they did not clear themselves from eating — on the contrary they prepare for another eating — if so Birkat HaMazon does not help at all; they have nothing to rely on and act against the Talmud per all views; and one who fears God should refrain from sitting with those not scrupulous in this in one gathering.
turei-zahav.2#_: And some are stringent even in meat after cheese. Explanation: to wait six hours; and measure of hard cheese that Rama mentioned means six months passed on it or it is wormy — so Orach Chaim; and he wrote there there is no prohibition in meat after cheese, for only taste of meat in the mouth, since its essence is called meat, is subject to decree lest basar b'chalav — nevertheless from piety one should be scrupulous, end of his words; and it appears to me (even) for Rambam's reason I mentioned at the beginning of the siman that eating cheese after meat is because of meat between the teeth, but for taste drawn from meat in the mouth we are not concerned — one may say here for any cheese there is no prohibition to eat meat after it, for also meat between the teeth is not called meat unless the verse revealed "the meat is still between his teeth" as in the Gemara — but cheese between the teeth is not cheese at all; and for the reason I mentioned that it is because of fat, it is plain to forbid also wormy cheese whose taste lingers long in the mouth — if so one should be stringent; but it appears to me specifically wormy cheese one should be stringent so, and it is by law from the reason we mentioned; but aged cheese that is not wormy and was not made from milk set in the stomach to curdle milk but from mere milk and dried, or one eats butter — one should not be stringent more than wiping, cleaning teeth, rinsing mouth and hands, except one who practices added abstinence and scrupulousness — so it appears to me.
turei-zahav.3#_: And fat of meat, etc. And it is written in Tur Chaadash general rule 77 in name of Hagahot ShaDa that even with goose fat one should be stringent so; and in Beit Yosef in Orach Chaim siman 173 he wrote in name of Hagahot Maimoniyot that meat broth has the law of meat; and Rabbenu Yonah in chapter Elu Devarim wrote it has the law of a meat dish since it is clear, but if thick like vegetables it has the law of meat.
turei-zahav.4#א: However through sticking, etc. This refers to what was written that one wants to cut cheese with a meat knife; but what was written that it is forbidden to cut bread, etc. — one need only wipe the knife as appears in Beit Yosef in what he wrote in name of Orach Chaim in name of Rabbenu Shimshon — and there the reason is noten taam bar noten taam; and for us need not this, for it is explained in siman 96 that specifically with a sharp thing they say it absorbs because of pressure of the knife.
turei-zahav.4#ב: But already they practice, etc. It appears his intent: according to the custom it is forbidden to cut cheese with a meat knife even through sticking in the ground, for so they were stringent on themselves to take a separate knife for cheese; but nevertheless to cut bread with it to eat cheese — in this we may well rely on wiping it first — as it appears to me, plain.

beur-hagra.1#א: Even of, etc. — as explained that aggra fowl after cheese is from R' Yitzchak's challenge and the tanna of aggra, etc.; Tosafot there pressed this only that at first for meat there is no difference, and therefore aggra after cheese is so.
beur-hagra.1#ב: Until he waits, etc. — for the morning meal of a Torah scholar is at the sixth hour as written in chapter 1 of Shabbat (10a) and Pesachim, and Shmuel said from the meal, etc.; and he states the law, for he called himself sick for not making a fence to be stringent. Rif, see there.
beur-hagra.1#ג: And even if, etc. and one who chews for a child, etc. — Rambam wrote the reason because of meat between the teeth that is not digested until six hours — and therefore it would be permitted after six hours; and Tur wrote the reason because meat expels fat and draws taste a long time — and therefore the chewer need not wait; and Tur wrote to be stringent like both explanations.
beur-hagra.1#ד: And if he found, etc. — although it does not draw taste, it is no worse than cheese which also does not draw taste — therefore permitted, etc.
beur-hagra.1#ה: And some say, etc. — as Tosafot explain there s.v. for the meal, etc.
beur-hagra.1#ו: And the custom, etc. however, etc. — built on Zohar parashat Mishpatim: whoever eats this food as one or in one time or in one meal, etc.
beur-hagra.1#ז: And if he found, etc. — Gemara as above.
beur-hagra.1#ח: And some say there is no, etc. — as Tosafot wrote there if one cleared, etc., and this is not clearing — Atzei Etz Chaim.
beur-hagra.2#א: (Lekut) And must wipe his mouth and rinse it. But Rashba explained one of them suffices — for otherwise why did Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel leave the other; and similarly aggra why leave rinsing (end).
beur-hagra.2#ב: And afterward he rinses. Some say afterward. Beit Yosef and so in the Gemara.
beur-hagra.2#ג: And some are stringent, etc. And so from the Zohar cited. Beit Yosef. And this is not as arguing with the Gemara, for they were stringent on themselves also regarding the permitted as written "I am sick," etc.
beur-hagra.3#א: One who ate, etc. but, etc. — Tosafot there s.v. for wiping and Mefaresh, etc.
beur-hagra.3#ב: And there are, etc. — per R' Shmuel there that specifically when both are of meat or both of cheese it is optional.
beur-hagra.3#ג: And fat, etc. — not like Rambam's words because of meat between the teeth but like Tur's explanation. Rashba there.
beur-hagra.3#ד: And they practice, etc. — as R' Shmuel explains there.
beur-hagra.3#ה: However, etc. — as R' Shmuel as above.
beur-hagra.3#ו: Waiter, etc. — Rashi 107b s.v. that he is busy, etc. and Shach.
beur-hagra.4#א: One who ate, etc. — Yerushalmi (chapter 6 of Pesachim): the law of one who ate chavitz and wants to eat kutach — he clears crumbs.
beur-hagra.4#ב: And forbidden, etc. — from the Yerushalmi cited and as written in Mishnah seif 7:2 and Gemara there, provided not, etc. — although the peel, etc.
beur-hagra.4#ג: And all the more, etc. — as written above siman 112:1 radish dragged, etc. and as written end of seif 96.
beur-hagra.4#ד: However, etc. — as written end of Avodah Zarah.

kereti.1#א: And even of wild animal — this is only custom as Rosh wrote, but by law it is permitted as written in Peleti, proof from Tosafot.
kereti.1#ב: Six hours — and for Rambam the reason that within six hours most meat is still between the teeth; and see Peleti what he wrote that do not challenge him from the Gemara.
kereti.1#ג: And if he found afterward — and when he removes it need not wait from then six hours.
kereti.1#ד: To rinse his mouth — and the same is mouth-wiping; and Rama abbreviated — so many Acharonim.
kereti.1#ה: And recited Birkat HaMazon — the same is final blessing where Birkat HaMazon is not required, for in any case there is clearing from what he ate and it is not like one who eats in a bundle.
kereti.1#ו: One hour — Peri Chadash wrote they have support from Zohar; and see Peleti I wrote the Zohar does not imply at all except one hour and six hours depends on dispute in Orach Chaim siman 184; and Peri Chadash's view in winter days is short — four hours from midday until evening suffices; and see Peleti I wrote this is not so; and if they come to be precise they should add more than six hours — therefore the essence is six hours and one should not add or subtract.
kereti.1#ז: And they are not scrupulous — Taz picked a quarrel with those not scrupulous; and see Peleti what he wrote they are correct and there is no reason to be scrupulous.
kereti.2#א: If it is at night — and if he has a good lamp like a torch, night is judged like day — Maharshal and Acharonim.
kereti.2#ב: At night — and if he ate meat first and they practice without waiting six hours, nevertheless he needs washing even by day lest something stuck to the hands; and see Peleti I proved this from Tosafot, see there.
kereti.2#ג: To wash them — and Acharonim brought liquids are not fit for him — so Raavad; and Maharshal permits; and see Peleti I brought proof from Tosafot for Raavad.
kereti.2#ד: Wild animal — even though wild animal is d'rabbanan and resembles fowl, nevertheless in its substance it resembles domestic animal and also sticks to hands and mouth like domestic animal.
kereti.2#ה: Without wiping — Beit Yosef brought in name of Zohar to be stringent for one who eats cheese after fowl; and Peri Chadash permits; and Zohar's words are not comfortable; but nevertheless Beit Yosef's words are not comfortable except Zohar deals with eating them together.
kereti.3#א: And fat of meat — even though it does not fit Rambam's reason of meat between teeth, it is forbidden because of lo plug; and the same for fat of fowl.
kereti.3#ב: Its law is like meat — and meat broth if clear has law of dish; if thick it has law of meat — Beit Yosef Orach Chaim.
kereti.3#ג: Waiter, etc. — see Acharonim what they wrote on this; and see Peleti what I wrote to resolve.
kereti.4#_: Forbidden to cut — noten taam bar noten taam is forbidden l'chatchila; and also because of the majority dry and something sticks in the eye.

kaf-hachayim.1#_: (1) [Seif 1] One who ate meat, even of wild animal and fowl, etc. — meaning they are d'rabbanan as written in siman 87 seif 3 Shach s.k. 1. For the plain understanding, section 1.
kaf-hachayim.2#_: (2) There. Until he waits six hours. And within the time, even if there is no meat between the teeth it is forbidden because meat expels fat and draws taste a long time; and therefore the reason if they only chewed for a child need not wait since they did not eat it does not impart taste. Rambam gave reason for waiting because of meat between the teeth; per his words after waiting the measure it is permitted even if meat remains between the teeth; and one who chews for a child must wait; and good to follow stringencies of both reasons. Tur. Taz s.k. 1. Shach s.k. 2. And this too Shulchan Aruch ruled like both stringencies.
kaf-hachayim.3#_: (3) And if one chews for a child a dish that has fat — apparently for all explanations need not wait, for there is no drawing since he did not eat and no meat between teeth; nevertheless one should be stringent to wait six hours because of lo plug and holy Israel should not breach the fence. Mishnat Zion section 1. Birkat Chaim in Shaarei Yosher section 12. Pithei Teshuvah section 1. Zivchei Tzedek section 4.
kaf-hachayim.4#_: (4) And specifically chewing; but if he tasted on his tongue and expelled immediately — need not wait according to all. Also if he took a piece of meat into his mouth and immediately returned it whole — need not wait; and all the more if he tasted fat and expelled — need not wait — Maharshak, glosses on Peri Megadim on Niddah dreams end of Ashlei Raverei. Zivchei Tzedek section 5.

mateh-yehonatan.1#_: (siman 89 seif 1 in the gloss) And some say need not wait six hours only, etc. And permitted through wiping and rinsing; and that wiping and rinsing are required even after Birkat HaMazon can be proven from the Talmud chapter 25 daf 107b s.v. fowl and cheese that he wrote there: say — how does it challenge from cheese first to meat later to cheese? And one may say it challenges thus: words of aggra imply fowl and cheese are eaten at an apikores meal without netilat yadayim and without wiping; but for other meat netilat yadayim is required — and how if meat first: even with netilat yadayim and mouth-wiping it does not suffice until another meal — unless from cheese first, end of his words; and if so it must be that Tosafot hold even for another meal wiping is required — otherwise it should have said we do not find wiping and rinsing; or that for cheese first too wiping and rinsing are required as Rama wrote there; but without Birkat HaMazon certainly waiting one hour does not help. And Magen Avraham in Orach Chaim wrote even for meat after cheese Birkat HaMazon is required; and it appears not like my view, for he says what are intermediate waters between meat and cheese — optional, meaning within the meal; and if so it must be Birkat HaMazon is not required — otherwise there is no case for intermediate waters to be optional at all, for before Birkat HaMazon one needs mayim acharonim at least — if so intermediate waters are without need; or Birkat HaMazon is not required at all between cheese and meat.
mateh-yehonatan.2#_: (there seif 2) Must wash them. See Shach s.k. 10 who brought in name of Maharshal that intermediate waters are invalid in other liquids, etc.; and from the Talmud it is proven like Raavad who wrote in Orach Chaim that I brought above in section 1, and so: Rabbenu Tam explains one who ate meat is forbidden to eat cheese — meaning without netilat yadayim and mouth-wiping, etc.; and Mar Ukva who does not eat until another meal without netilat yadayim and mouth-wiping — according to his reasoning how is it sensible to say he does not eat until another meal without netilat yadayim and mouth-wiping, for in any case he must wash for Birkat HaMazon first and mayim acharonim are obligatory — so he has netilat yadayim; if so it must be Tosafot hold intermediate waters are invalid in other liquids and mayim acharonim are valid — and therefore even if he washed in other liquids for mayim acharonim, for intermediate waters it does not help at all.
mateh-yehonatan.3#_: (there seif 3 in the gloss) Waiter, etc. at the meal need not netilat yadayim. See Shach s.k. 20 and Peri Chadash who wondered at Beit Yosef and Rama who copied Rashi here that Rashi deals only with netilat yadayim at the meal; but wherever all netilat yadayim is because of what sticks to hands — certainly the waiter too needs netilat yadayim, see there; and in my humble opinion it appears to resolve: Beit Yosef did not intend to bring proof that the waiter even though he handles food need not netilat yadayim — that is plain, for from where would we say if one handles basar b'chalav not at eating time he needs netilat yadayim; or for this Beit Yosef did not need proof at all, for certainly he need not any netilat yadayim, for it teaches only about one who eats meat or milk — only that for the waiter one might say he properly needs netilat yadayim lest he come to eat from it; on this he properly brings proof from Rashi that we are not concerned lest he eat — and Beit Yosef's words are correct — investigate.

nekudot-hakesef.1#_: (siman 89 s.k. 6) This refers. This is not so, as explained explicitly in Torat Chatat general rule 76 law 6 that even to cut bread with it to eat with cheese requires sticking — and what is written in law 7 is not so; and what he wrote and for us need not this, etc. is not a matter, for we do not forbid here because of actual absorption, for it is cold with cold, but because the knife's grease coats its face and since its use is frequent wiping does not suffice. And Maharshal is stringent here that even sticking does not help — and see Shach s.k. 20.

peleti.1#א: Even of wild animal and fowl — Rosh wrote so they practice; but by law it appears Tosafot and Rosh do not hold so, for they challenged lest the Gemara not be established for aggra that the master said fowl and cheese are eaten at an apikores meal — he ate fowl meat first and afterward cheese — and resolved: if so it implies domestic animal meat requires wiping — even waiting six hours requires, see there — and they did not resolve briefly how one eats at an apikores meal — he needs six hours — and how is apikores meal relevant — only certainly for fowl Tosafot hold need not; therefore they brought all proofs from precision of domestic animal.
peleti.1#ב: If there is meat between the teeth — Tur implies for Rambam he gave reason for waiting six hours because of meat between teeth — implies afterward it is considered digested; and Peri Chadash challenged: but in the Gemara they asked about meat between teeth and answered meat between them, etc., see there; and it appears from this proof he relied on six hours, for the measure between meal and meal is six hours and the reason is that within this time he has no appetite to eat; but when six hours pass he has appetite as explained in Orach Chaim measure of digestion — and this is the Gemara's question about between teeth how long to wait until digested — and it answered from scripture "the meat is still between their teeth," etc., and in Psalms "they were not yet sated, still they eat in their mouth" — learn still not digested; and similarly in midrash "before the food was digested" — as explained in Orach Chaim there is no appetite to eat — behold this measure of between teeth is measure before digestion of food — otherwise how could scripture state plainly meat between them implying later time — it would be immediately before digestion; and it must be both are one, for all time of digestion is called meat and afterward not — and it is clear and plain.
peleti.1#ג: After eating meat one hour — Peri Chadash's view to give reason for this custom from Zohar that says do not eat one time — this is not so, for language of one time means one period and is not measured in hours of the world but a time — and from afternoon until evening is also called one time; but it appears this is whether to wait one hour or six hours they disagree about digestion — see Orach Chaim siman 184 Magen Avraham s.k. 9: beginning of digestion is about an hour and a fifth and end of digestion six hours; the lenient counted this as measure of beginning of digestion for Birkat HaMazon so no longer need Birkat HaMazon — if so also for this it is already digested and gone and therefore permitted to eat — and almost their reasons are sensible; the stringent follow end of digestion which is six hours as Magen Avraham wrote there — therefore six hours waiting is required — and this is clear. And here we learn we require full six hours and not like Peri Chadash to say in short winter days one eats at noon and can eat cheese at evening — for that is between meal and meal, for per my words we require measure of digestion. And also what did he tell us that in winter if one eats at noon the meal time is immediately evening — certainly they eat when many hours passed at night — can digestion or meat taste pass in winter and shortest days more than long days? There is nothing to this; and in truth on the contrary there is room to be stringent, for four hours is meal time for all — nevertheless they eat only at evening as is known — and if they want to be precise they should add more than six hours; therefore the essence is six hours without adding or subtracting.
peleti.1#ד: But they are not scrupulous in this — and Taz picked a quarrel; and I did not understand the reason of those who forbid, for the whole matter of not eating meat and cheese together is because of heker lest they eat meat and milk together — what of it if he intends to bless in order to eat cheese afterward — in the end there is heker; and on the contrary if his intent is only to bless in order to eat cheese there is greater heker — how would he eat together; and also he cannot eat if not with a break of Birkat HaMazon — therefore I did not know what stringency is here.
peleti.2#_: And must, etc. — see Shach s.k. 16 who brought Raavad disqualifies liquids and Maharshal permits; and Tosafot s.v. fowl wrote per Rabbenu Tam's view need not wait from meal to meal — meaning without wiping and netilat yadayim, etc.; and it is difficult: the first is not difficult, for in the second meal he had to wash anyway for eating — he truly did not wash and therefore did not eat until another meal — and then he washed; but difficult: in the first meal at Birkat HaMazon he had to take mayim acharonim — so he already had netilat yadayim; strained to say the meal dealt with is bread in a pouch, etc. that need no netilat yadayim — that is not called a meal; and if he fixed a meal he must bless and also mayim acharonim — therefore must be they were accustomed to wash in other liquids like passing Sodomite salt — and this does not help intermediate waters between meat and cheese to remove oiliness — and Raavad's words are compelled; and perhaps Raavad inferred from this — investigate. And it appears what we distinguish between day and night is for cheese first; but for meat first for those who do not wait six hours, even by day washing is required lest something stuck — and with this Rabbenu Tam's words are understood: he wrote one who ate meat first is forbidden to eat cheese after without rinsing and wiping; but one who ate cheese first need not netilat yadayim nor wiping — Maharsha wondered: but netilat yadayim we say for Rabbenu Tam is required even for cheese first — and see what I wrote in his answer.
peleti.3#_: However waiter, etc. — Shach and Acharonim wondered this was said only for netilat yadayim at the meal and not for intermediate waters; and it appears Beit Yosef heaven forbid was not mistaken, only he held we do not find anywhere they enacted for one who touches meat in general not to touch cheese until he washes; and if you think so — why did they say for one who ate meat netilat yadayim is required for cheese — even touching would require netilat yadayim; only certainly they enacted only for the eater whose hands are very soiled, and also at eating they were more concerned with extra distance; and therefore the waiter who only touches is permitted — only lest you say they decreed lest he eat; on this he brings proof we see in netilat yadayim they did not decree so — learn they did not decree; and therefore here too no decree — and we return to the rule that we do not forbid touching what we never found — this is Beit Yosef's intent, it appears to me.

pitchei-teshuva.1#_: Six hours. See Shach: if one chews for a child a dish with fat — apparently for all explanations need not wait, for no drawing since he did not eat and no meat between teeth; nevertheless Pri Megadim wrote to be stringent to wait six hours because of lo plug and not to breach the fence.
pitchei-teshuva.2#_: They are not scrupulous in this. Avodat HaTaharah end s.k. 3 in name of Taz; and see Bikkur Shor in his novellae on Chullin daf 105 who disagrees and raised that one should not protest the lenient whom Rama brought — they have what to rely on, see there.
pitchei-teshuva.3#_: Six hours. Avodat HaTaharah of Maharit — if they are seasonal hours; and see Knesset HaGedolah and Pri Megadim and Chochmat Adam who agreed with Kenesset HaGedolah they are not seasonal, see there — and so is the custom. [And see responsum Chasam Sofer siman 73: a sick person drinking milk for healing even if only slightly ill need not wait after eating meat more than an hour, and after he already recited Birkat HaMazon he may drink and it will settle for him, see there.]
pitchei-teshuva.4#_: He should examine. Avodat HaTaharah in name of Peri Chadash; and in Pri Megadim wrote it is fit to be stringent in a matter without effort, see there.

rabbi-akiva-eiger-yd.1#_: (siman 89 Shach s.k. 5) If he did not clear and recite Birkat HaMazon — even the entire day — and for this Magen Avraham agreed (siman 196 s.k. 5).
rabbi-akiva-eiger-yd.2#_: (section 1 in the gloss) After eating meat for cheese. Possibly he was precise that after eating one is stringent, but after chewing without eating some permit completely — do not wait six hours.
rabbi-akiva-eiger-yd.3#_: (seif 3 in the gloss) And some require netilat yadayim. It appears without wiping and rinsing; and what Rama wrote not to eat cheese after a meat dish means cheese in substance, but a cheese dish after a meat dish is permitted with netilat yadayim alone; however in Tur Chaadash as Pithei Megadim explained Menachem Tzioni letter 10 his view there for meat dish then cheese dish requires also wiping and rinsing, and when reversed cheese first then meat wiping alone suffices; and in Menachem Tzioni there letter 11 he wrote in name of Maharshal: now they practice prohibition even for cheese dish after meat dish — hard to be lenient and appear before them while cleared and recited, end of his words.
rabbi-akiva-eiger-yd.4#_: (Shach s.k. 16) that it is noten taam bar noten taam. In my humble opinion one may say there is a difference: even in one's own vinegar that is sharp in a meat bowl — there is no noten taam bar noten taam — nevertheless permitted to eat cheese after it.

yad-avraham.1#_: (siman 89 seif 2) Must wipe his mouth and rinse it. And so Tur: some soak bread in wine or water and eat it, and it counts for wiping and rinsing; and better each separately, end of his words. And see siman 116 seif 3 in the gloss regarding washing hands and mouth between fish and meat — and the same here.
yad-avraham.2#_: (there seif 3 in the gloss) Not to eat cheese after a meat dish like after meat itself. Logical proof shows not specifically cheese itself but even a cheese dish after a meat dish they practiced to be stringent — so Maharshal; but from the gloss below it does not appear to be stringent in this; and so Menachem Tzioni general rule 77 and Sefer Or Zarua in Orach Chaim siman 173 — this is the view of the gloss that wiping and rinsing help.
yad-avraham.3#_: (there) However if there is no meat in the dish only it was cooked in a meat pot — permitted to eat cheese after it. Shach wrote below siman 95 it will be explained that even to eat with cheese is permitted as noten taam bar noten taam of permitted taste; and it appears it comes to teach us even if the pot is not washed well, see there. And one of the Acharonim s.k. 14 wrote — and I do not understand, for Rama there forbids. And Menachem Tzioni and Sefer Or Zarua already preceded there; and one may say Shach infers from Beit Yosef who is the source of this law that the gloss wrote for us l'chatchila noten taam bar noten taam is permitted — what does it teach us; and he resolved it teaches even if the pot is not washed — if so the same for us as in Pri Megadim; and it must deal even when we know there was not sixty against the fat — for if presumed we say there was sixty as Menachem Tzioni wrote — if so still what to say; however from Beit Yosef's language in Orach Chaim siman 173 it appears he speaks for those who forbid, since he concludes and if permitted to eat with cheese R' Yehuda siman 95; and Sefer Or Zarua is stringent; and see Sefer Bal Yei'ader who wrote if the substance imparts taste in the dish it is forbidden.
yad-avraham.4#_: (there seif 4) Forbidden to eat cheese on a cloth where they ate meat. It appears on a long cloth it is permitted to eat on one side meat and on the other side cheese. Proof from what Mechaber wrote above siman 88 regarding two people eating one meat and one cheese on one cloth — if there is a heker between them it is permitted. And another proof from the Gemara chapter 25b (daf 107) and so Taz wrote siman 91: one wraps meat and cheese in one cloth provided they do not touch each other — investigate.

yad-ephraim.1#_: After eating meat one hour. Avodat HaTaharah; and see Turei Megadim in name of Peri Chadash; and see Gan HaMelekh section 154: his view is always to estimate by time and always must wait a quarter of the day; in summer when the day is long wait much, in winter little, see there — and in truth they did not practice so, only wait six hours which is a quarter of the day whether summer or winter; and where there is danger of illness one may rely on Peri Chadash.
